messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple serving nodes in us-west-2 are flapping. Symptoms aggregated: container restarts, OOM events in userland, and repeated CUDA illegal memory access logs from the runtime. Auto-escalation -> P1. Start triage.

sara (oncall): Got it, I'm on it. Which pools are affected? Any customer-facing errors reported?

deepak (eng-runtime): Affected pool: inference-pool-usw2-gpu. Pattern: nodes start evicting pods, container restarts, then within 10-30s we see gpu driver messages + `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in the runtime logs. Started ~2845501100 and periodically since.

kai (eng-sre): Seeing node flaps on 3 distinct hosts: gw-usw2-3a-12, gw-usw2-3a-18, gw-usw2-3b-05. Kernel dmesg (excerpt):

```
[  842.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID: 23456, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  842.123459] kworker/3:2: segfault at 0 ip 00007fbd... sp 00007ffd... error 4 in libc-2.31.so[7fbd...]
[  842.123462] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU reported an illegal memory access at 0x7f2b3c4a0000
```

kai (eng-sre): Also seeing repeated OOM-killer invocations in kernel logs before GPU message. Could be a race between container OOM and GPU driver reclaim.

alice (support): Customers: a handful of high-throughput tenants saw 5xxs and timeouts for ~30-90s. I have an open ticket from acme-inc reporting errors in embed API. Will notify them we're investigating.

ben (infra): Let's cordon the affected nodes and drain any remaining pods. Recommend immediate mitigation: cordon + drain, and re-route traffic to cpu-fallback nodes + scale out gpu pool with fresh nodes.

sara (oncall): Agreed. ben, can you run the cordon/drain? deepak, can runtime enable CPU fallback for the affected model routes?

ben (infra): Running: `kubectl cordon gw-usw2-3a-12 && kubectl drain gw-usw2-3a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

ops-bot: Drain started for gw-usw2-3a-12. 6 pods evicted.

ben (infra): Done for 3a-12 and 3a-18. 3b-05 still flapping, drain failing due to pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff.

deepak (eng-runtime): Enabling CPU fallback on the model route now (force cpu_fallback=true) for the top-10 affected customers. Rolling config via rollout ID r-2026-03-15-01. That will send new traffic to CPU variants.

sara (oncall): Good. Any quick config to reduce memory pressure while we stabilize?

deepak (eng-runtime): Lowering batch size and max-concurrency for the GPU replicas: set BATCH_SIZE=1, MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 for the pool. Pushing a config change now. Should reduce GPU memory footprint per-request.

kai (eng-sre): Also recommend setting eviction threshold higher temporarily: kubelet --eviction-hard=memory.available<200Mi -> bump to 150Mi? (we'll be careful). I'll coordinate with infra.

ben (infra): Applied node cordon. For stuck pods on 3b-05 I'm going to force delete and then isolate the node. `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0 <pod>`

alice (support): Customer impact update: acme-inc reported 12 failed requests in last 10m; their latency spikes correspond with the nodes flapping. Communicated we have a mitigation in place (cpu-fallback + config changes).

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation actions logged: nodes cordoned, drains initiated, cpu-fallback enabled, batch-size reduced. Keep thread updated.

ben (infra): For root cause evidence, I pulled dmesg and a mini coredump from gw-usw2-3b-05. Attaching snippet:

```
== begin nvidia log ==
E Mon Mar 15 08:41:04 2026
NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU panic: Xid 79
NVRM: GPU illegal memory access at 0x7f2b3c4a0000
NVRM: GPU context: 0x7fabcde0
== end nvidia log ==
```

ben (infra): Also saw container OOM log right before: `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` in model-worker PID 23456.

deepak (eng-runtime): That lines up with our hypothesis: container OOM triggers some reclamation path that races with the NVIDIA driver memory free leading to an illegal access in kernel/driver when the runtime later touches freed GPU pointers (we saw stale device pointers in logs).

kai (eng-sre): Repro plan: try to artificially trigger OOM on a staged node with same kernel and nvidia driver versions, reproduce the race by killing the process after it issues cudaFree. If reproducible, vendor escalation.

tim (cust-succ): Sending status note to top-tier customers now. Will include that we have fallbacks in place and are monitoring.

sara (oncall): On-call handover: I'm handing to ben for the next 90 minutes to run recovery actions. Ben, you own the runbook: cordon/drain, collect logs, and coordinate with eng-runtime for reproductions. I'll update incident channel every 15 mins.

ben (infra): Acknowledged. Running node reboots on the 2 isolated hosts to clear driver state.

deepak (eng-runtime): Captured additional runtime trace pointing to potential use-after-free in our GPU slab allocator: stack: runtime::alloc_gpu_mem -> cudaMalloc -> model_worker->process_request -> cudaMemcpy -> crash. I'll create deterministic instrumentation in staging to guard allocations and add address-sanitizer like checks where possible.

kai (eng-sre): For immediate safety, let's enable automatic fallback policy for all customers on the faulty 3-node AZ until we have a vendor fix or kernel patch. Also open an urgent ticket with NVIDIA with dmesg, Xid logs, kernel versions, and coredumps.

alice (support): I'll update the tickets and include the mitigation timeline and customer-facing note.

incident-bot: :information_source: Next steps logged: 1) Reproduce in staging w/ same kernel/driver/model; 2) Collect full coredumps + nv-trace; 3) Open vendor escalation; 4) Develop hotpatch/workaround (safe free path).

ben (infra): Reboots finished. Nodes came back healthy. Drained nodes have been reintroduced one at a time with monitoring. We'll keep CPU fallback on until root cause cleared.

deepak (eng-runtime): Putting a temporary guard in runtime to avoid touching GPU pointers after OOM handling path completes. Patch pushed to rollout canary.

sara (oncall): Thanks team. Ben you'll continue monitoring; deepak/kai follow up on repro and vendor escalation. I'll do the customer comms cadence. Handing out of on-call in 10m to next rotation.

alice (support): Customers notified. Some asked for ETA; I'll say 3-6 hours while we reproduce and validate fix.

ben (infra): Monitoring: error rate down to baseline for affected tenants after fallback. No new Xid 79 after reboots + patch canary so far.

deepak (eng-runtime): Logging full allocation traces and will share artifact links in follow-up thread. For now, can everyone drop any collected logs in the incident S3 bucket: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2845501234/ (dmesg, runtime logs, coredumps, nv-trace).

kai (eng-sre): Escalated to NVIDIA with ticket #NV-2026-4578. Attached Xid logs and minimal repro steps.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident P1 mitigated (traffic routed to fallback, nodes stabilized). Remaining work: root cause verification and vendor patch.

sara (oncall): Closing loop for now. If error spikes recur reopen. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
